title: The Galaxy-Sized Cosmic Ghost
description: Hanny's Voorwerp is a massive green structure glowing in deep space, but its power source died over 100,000 years ago.

beats.text: A galaxy-sized green cloud is glowing with no visible power source.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope photograph of Hanny's Voorwerp and the galaxy IC 2497, 2010

beats.text: Discovered by Dutch schoolteacher Hanny van Arkel, this phantom sits near the galaxy IC 2497.
beats.visual: photograph of Dutch schoolteacher Hanny van Arkel, 2008

beats.text: Located 650 million light-years away in Leo Minor, the structure shines with a striking green glow.
beats.visual: Sloan Digital Sky Survey wide field view of the constellation Leo Minor, 2007

beats.text: Astronomers investigated with the Hubble Space Telescope and found an apparent hole 20,000 light-years wide.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image showing the apparent hole in Hanny's Voorwerp, 2010

beats.text: Yet, nothing inside the massive structure was producing enough energy to light it up.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope close-up of the gas filaments in Hanny's Voorwerp, 2010

beats.text: The explanation is terrifying: we are looking at the ghost of a dead quasar.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a glowing gas cloud illuminated by a distant quasar beam, 2012

beats.text: Over 100,000 years ago, a supermassive black hole in IC 2497 blasted a monstrous beam.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of a supermassive black hole powering a brilliant active galactic nucleus, 2010
queries: supermassive black hole jet accretion disk

beats.text: That powerhouse has since faded dramatically, but its light is still traveling across deep space.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a faded quasar leaving behind a lingering ionization echo, 2013

beats.text: Its dead central engine left behind a lingering cosmic ghost.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope wide field view of Hanny's Voorwerp and IC 2497, 2010
